records.reason: m167 at 20/1 is a strong-ratio non-donor carbonyl gate control. It tests whether PE-rich conditions alone generate a late tail, contrasting severe measured carbonyl failures such as d1172a49fca1e196a59f.
m25 at 0/1 provides an ordinary multifunctional acceptor anchor at weak solvent strength. It helps constrain corrections learned from severe polar rows and retain central calibration.
The non-donor aldehyde m184 at 10/1 tests whether an intermediate PE-rich condition begins a scaffold-specific aldehyde tail, complementing ordinary and severe carbonyl behavior.
m117 at 2/1 and high loading amount samples the intermediate response of a donor-containing multifunctional aldehyde. It can separate solvent-strength curvature from loading effects.
m77 at 0/1 is a weak-condition halogenated ester control without a donor. Its label protects the ordinary response surface while donor-rich and multifunctional tails are repaired.
m208 at 10/1 and high loading tests whether a phenolic donor scaffold begins a broad completion tail at intermediate PE enrichment, extending the severe donor observation 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf.
The m117 20/1 point extends the same polar aldehyde family into a stronger condition. It can locate a threshold and test whether V2 changes more sharply than V1.
m182 at 5/1 probes a fused carbonyl scaffold in an intermediate regime. It tests whether broad endpoint behavior transfers from severe carbonyl rows or remains scaffold-local.
m74 at 10/1 in PE samples a multi-acceptor ester under stronger solvent and moderate loading. It provides an intermediate control between ordinary ester behavior and late polar tails.
m111 at 2/1 is a neutral methoxy halogenated aromatic control. It helps determine whether aromatic ether chemistry remains in the central regime rather than inheriting donor-driven tail corrections.
m95 at 2/1 supplies a low-ratio carbonyl anchor. Together with measured higher-ratio m95 rows, it helps locate onset of endpoint broadening.
m122 at 1/1 is a neutral aromatic ether control with distinct halogenation and loading. It tests transfer of ordinary calibration across weak conditions and non-donor structures.
m32 at 0/1 provides a simple ketone anchor under weak solvent strength. It separates routine carbonyl behavior from the large late errors in multifunctional carbonyl rows.
m55 at 20/1 in PE tests a non-donor aromatic ester in a strong-ratio condition. Its label can reveal whether high PE ratio alone is sufficient for a broad completion interval.
m211 at 0/1 is a weak-condition pyridyl aromatic control. It anchors nitrogen-containing chemistry before testing the high-ratio regime and helps avoid a universal nitrogen correction.
m40 at 2/1 provides central ketone coverage at moderate loading. It complements the much later measured high-ratio m40 behavior in 4e93e36ab850bab3d594 and constrains condition curvature.
m104 at 20/1 tests a donor-containing amino ester in a strong-ratio regime. It probes whether nitrogen and donor interactions produce the same completion tail as measured severe polar rows.
m153 is a non-donor halogenated aromatic control at 1/1. It tests ordinary calibration across high molecular weight and halogen content without a hydrogen-bond donor.
m57 at 50/1 is a strong-ratio neutral hydrocarbon-like control. It directly tests whether PE enrichment alone creates a late tail, complementing measured neutral m57 behavior.
m155 at 1/1 supplies another neutral halogenated aromatic point with a distinct loading amount. It protects central calibration against overfitting rare tail labels.
m37 at 1/1 probes a nitro-containing ketone with unusually broad model behavior. Its label can distinguish a nitrogen or polar interaction effect from ordinary aromatic carbonyl variation.

m155 at 50/1 extends the neutral halogenated control to a strong ratio. Comparing it with the weak-condition m155 point tests whether a condition-only tail is present without donors or strong acceptor clusters.
m151 at 20/1 adds a neutral heavy-halogen aromatic point in a PE-rich condition. It tests whether molecular size and halogenation alone move rows into the late regime.
m14 at 2/1 is a hydrocarbon-like aromatic control at weak-to-moderate strength. It helps preserve the central nonpolar response surface while polar corrections are learned.
m46 at 10/1 tests a non-donor brominated ester at intermediate PE enrichment. It helps determine whether ester and halogen chemistry avoids the donor-rich completion-tail regime.

m193 at 10/1 and high loading probes a nitro aldehyde in a nitrogen-containing carbonyl regime. It tests whether N-rich carbonyls share the large endpoint errors seen in measured nitrogen-rich failures.
m116 at 0/1 is a weak-condition neutral dimethoxy aromatic control. It anchors ether-rich but non-donor chemistry against severe donor-containing and multifunctional tails.
m157 at 1/1 provides a heavy-halogen neutral control with distinct molecular weight and loading. It tests whether high heteroatom mass without hydrogen bonding requires a separate correction.
m58 at 0/1 adds a weak-condition phenolic donor anchor. It distinguishes ordinary low-strength donor behavior from the extreme high-ratio donor failure in 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf.
m44 at 50/1 tests a simple ketone at the strong-ratio end. It can reveal whether ordinary carbonyls develop a tail comparable to multifunctional carbonyls or remain structurally gated.
m121 at 20/1 in PE is a neutral anisole-like control under strong solvent enrichment. It tests whether a non-donor ether remains central.
m149 at 0/1 is a weak-condition heavy-halogen aromatic control. It extends neutral, non-donor coverage and helps prevent rare late-tail corrections from shifting ordinary halogenated rows.

hypotheses.content: PE-rich retention failures are condition-gated and scaffold-local; V2 can change more sharply than V1 rather than following one global polarity correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest errors remain concentrated in late carbonyl, donor-containing, and heteroatom-rich tails, while several neutral rows remain close. The model needs structural and condition gates rather than a global PE correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the new polar and carbonyl condition points show shared solvent thresholds or separate scaffold-specific transitions?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading volume interact with strongly retained scaffolds and can alter V1 and V2 asymmetrically, but the effect is not universal or monotone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Measured m177 and m125 rows show large amount- and volume-dependent endpoint changes, while several neutral controls do not. Additional high- and low-loading points can teach when the recorded loading features interact with scaffold and solvent strength.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are loading-related endpoint shifts reproducible within chemically related families, especially for polar and nitrogen-containing molecules?

hypotheses.content: High-ratio tail repair requires a structural gate: related non-donor or neutral rows can remain close while multifunctional carbonyl, donor, and heteroatom scaffolds fail badly.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The Row-distribution contains many ordinary neutral and non-donor rows, so an ungated tail correction could reduce overall accuracy even while repairing rare failures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the additional neutral, halogenated, ketone, and ester controls separate cleanly from donor-rich and multifunctional tail regimes?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing carbonyl and heteroaromatic families form a distinct high-retention regime with frequent V2 underprediction, although transfer across N-containing scaffolds is incomplete.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A nitrogen-sensitive representation or gate could repair large errors in several N-containing families while avoiding unnecessary corrections to rows that are already calibrated.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the new m37, m104, m193, and m211 measurements share endpoint behavior with the previously failing N-rich families after accounting for ratio and loading?

hypotheses.content: Neutral and weakly polar aromatic controls are expected to anchor the central response surface, so tail repair should be localized rather than propagated across the majority chemistry.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Central controls constrain retraining against overfitting rare late-retention examples and support generalization across common neutral and weakly polar rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected neutral controls remain calibrated at both weak and PE-rich conditions while tail corrections are localized?

hypotheses.content: Several acceptor-rich and heteroatom-containing scaffolds remain ordinary at low or intermediate PE ratio and develop a late V2 tail only beyond a scaffold-specific threshold.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local response curves can teach nonlinear condition effects and endpoint asymmetry, reducing the risk of interpolating a single global solvent-strength trend across chemically distinct scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do intermediate m95, m114, m184, and related condition points locate reproducible onset thresholds before the strongest PE-rich conditions?

feedback_interpretation: Recent labels strengthened the scaffold-local and endpoint-asymmetric tail interpretation. Severe failures remain concentrated in multifunctional carbonyl, donor-containing, nitrogen-rich, and selected heteroatom scaffolds, while neutral and weakly polar controls are often close. Loading effects remain unresolved because m177 and m125 show large changes but several matched neutral rows do not. The corrected batch therefore combines high-ratio tail probes, weak and intermediate controls, nitrogen-containing structures, and ordinary non-donor anchors.
batch_rationale: The batch uses condition-response probes to identify where retention transitions begin, including high-ratio donor, nitrogen, carbonyl, and non-donor candidates. It also includes weak-condition and neutral controls so the retrained model can learn a structural gate instead of applying a broad PE correction. Several loading amounts and volumes are represented across polar and nitrogen-containing structures, while simple ketones, esters, hydrocarbons, and halogenated aromatics preserve central calibration. This combination targets both rare high-error regions and the majority central Row-distribution, improving transfer of V1/V2 corrections across scaffold and condition space.
